info.headline: Read short sentences with pictures, charts, and tables.
info.summary: Starting readers work with 2–4 short sentences about familiar topics like school, home, plants, and animals. Every text comes with a picture, a labeled diagram, a pictograph, or a simple table. Students find key details, put short events in order, sort words, and match words to pictures.

I can match words to a picture.
I can put pictures and sentences in order.
I can read a simple chart or table.

activities.title: Amara's Garden
activities.skill: Finding a key detail with a picture
activities.directions: Look at the picture. Read the sentences. Choose the best answer.
activities.prompt: What does Amara water?
passage: Amara works in the school garden.
She waters the tomatoes with a green watering can.
The sunflowers are taller than Amara!

picture.alt: A girl pours water from a green watering can onto red tomato plants in a school garden. Tall yellow sunflowers grow next to her.

vocabulary: garden
a place where people grow plants
jardín: un lugar donde se cultivan plantas
water
to give water to a plant
regar: darle agua a una planta
tall
high from the bottom to the top
alto: que mide mucho de abajo hacia arriba
readFor: the name of a plant after it
activities.correct: Yes! The text says she waters the tomatoes, and the picture shows water falling on the red tomatoes.
activities.hint: Find the word waters in sentence 2. Read the next word.
activities.support: Point to each plant in the picture and say its name: tomatoes, sunflowers. Then find those words in the text.
activities.extension: Write one more sentence about the garden. Start with: The sunflowers are ___.

teacher.use: Warm-up for 'right there' detail questions with picture support.
teacher.function: Locating a key detail; matching a noun to an image.
teacher.lower: Read the sentences aloud and point to each plant as you name it.
teacher.onLevel: Students read independently and find the word that follows waters.
teacher.challenge: Students tell what Amara might do next in the garden.
teacher.noTech: Print the picture and text; students circle the plant Amara waters.
teacher.prompt: What would you grow in a school garden?

activities.title: From Egg to Frog
activities.skill: Putting events in order
activities.directions: Look at the picture of the frog's life. Read the sentences. Put the steps in order.
activities.prompt: Put the frog's life steps in order. Start with the first step.
passage: A frog starts life as a tiny egg in a pond.
The egg hatches into a tadpole with a long tail.
The tadpole grows four legs.
At last, it is a frog that can hop on land.

picture.alt: Four stages of a frog's life in a circle with arrows: frog eggs in water, a tadpole with a long tail, a tadpole with four legs, and a grown frog.

items.text: A frog starts as a tiny egg.
It is a frog that can hop on land.
The egg hatches into a tadpole.

vocabulary: egg
a small round thing a baby animal comes out of
huevo: cosa redonda de donde sale un animal bebé
tadpole
a baby frog that swims and has a tail
renacuajo: una rana bebé que nada y tiene cola
hatch
to come out of an egg
salir del huevo (eclosionar): cuando un animal sale del huevo
readFor: order words like starts and at last
what the frog looks like at each step
activities.correct: Great ordering! Egg, then tadpole, then a tadpole with legs, then a frog. The words starts and at last are clues.
activities.hint: Which sentence has the word starts? That is the first step. Which has at last?
activities.support: Follow the arrows in the picture with your finger. Say: egg, tadpole, legs, frog.
activities.extension: Tell the steps to a partner using first, next, then, and last.

teacher.use: Sequencing routine with a science life cycle (Grade 3 life science).
teacher.function: Ordering events; noticing signal words (starts, at last).
teacher.lower: Act out each stage with hands (small egg, wiggly tail, legs, hop).
teacher.onLevel: Students order the sentences independently and read them aloud.
teacher.challenge: Students compare the frog cycle to a butterfly's life cycle.
teacher.noTech: Cut the four sentences into strips; students order them on a desk.
teacher.prompt: What other animals change as they grow?

activities.title: At the Library
activities.skill: Clicking the sentence with a detail
activities.directions: Look at the picture. Read the sentences. Click one sentence.
activities.prompt: Click the sentence that tells what Kenji reads about.

picture.alt: A boy and a girl read at a big table in a library. The boy's book has a shark on the cover, and the girl's book has a moon on the cover. Bookshelves are behind them.

sentences.text: Kenji and his sister go to the library after school.
They sit at a big table.
Kenji reads a book about sharks.
His sister reads a book about the moon.

vocabulary: library
a place with many books you can borrow
biblioteca: un lugar con muchos libros que puedes pedir prestados
sister
a girl in your family with the same parents
hermana: una niña de tu familia con los mismos padres
shark
a big fish with sharp teeth
tiburón: un pez grande con dientes filosos
readFor: the words reads a book about
activities.correct: Yes! Sentence 3 says Kenji reads a book about sharks. In the picture, his book has a shark on it.
activities.hint: Find the sentence that has Kenji's name AND the word reads.
activities.support: Two sentences tell about reading. Which one is about Kenji, not his sister?
activities.extension: Which sentence tells what his sister reads about? Read it aloud.

teacher.use: Introduces hot-text (click the sentence) items with heavy picture support.
teacher.function: Locating a specific detail; distinguishing two similar sentences.
teacher.lower: Read each sentence aloud while pointing to the matching part of the picture.
teacher.onLevel: Students read and click on their own, then explain their choice.
teacher.challenge: Students write a new sentence: Kenji learns that sharks ___.
teacher.noTech: Print the sentences; students underline the one about Kenji's book.
teacher.prompt: What kind of book do you like to read at the library?

activities.title: Recycling Day
activities.skill: Sorting using details from a text
activities.directions: Look at the picture. Read the sentences. Sort each thing into the right bin.
activities.prompt: Where does each thing go? Sort it into the blue bin or the green bin.
passage: Our class recycles every Friday.
Paper goes in the blue bin.
Cans go in the green bin.

picture.alt: A blue recycling bin full of paper and a green recycling bin full of cans in a classroom.

vocabulary: recycle
to use old things again to make new things
reciclar: usar cosas viejas otra vez para hacer cosas nuevas
bin
a big box or can that holds things
contenedor: una caja o bote grande para guardar cosas
can
a metal container for food or drinks
lata: un envase de metal para comida o bebidas
frames: A ___ goes in the blue bin because it is paper.
A ___ goes in the green bin because it is a can.
activities.correct: Nice sorting! Paper things go in the blue bin, and cans go in the green bin, just like the text says.
activities.hint: Look for the word paper or can in each item. Then check which bin the text gives it.
activities.support: Say: paper = blue, can = green. Point to the bins in the picture as you sort.
activities.extension: Name one more thing from your classroom that can go in the blue bin.

teacher.use: Sorting routine tied to a classroom procedure text.
teacher.function: Classifying objects using two rules stated in the text.
teacher.lower: Bring a real paper and a clean can; sort them together first.
teacher.onLevel: Students sort all six items and say a frame for two of them.
teacher.challenge: Students add a third bin (plastic) and write the rule sentence.
teacher.noTech: Print item cards; students place them on a drawn blue bin and green bin.
teacher.prompt: Why is recycling good for our school?

activities.title: Parts of a Plant

activities.directions: Look at the labeled picture. Read the sentences. Choose the best answer.
activities.prompt: What do the roots do?
passage: A plant has four main parts.
The roots are under the soil, and they take in water.
The leaves use sunlight to make food.

the parts of a plant under the ground

soil
dirt where plants grow
tierra (suelo): donde crecen las plantas
leaves
the flat green parts of a plant
hojas: las partes verdes y planas de una planta
activities.correct: Correct! The text says the roots are under the soil and take in water. The label shows where the roots are.
activities.hint: Find the word roots in the text. What do they take in?
activities.support: Point to the label roots on the picture. Then find roots in sentence 2 and read to the end.
activities.extension: What do the leaves do? Say it with the frame: The leaves ___.

teacher.use: Text-feature routine: labels on a science diagram (Grade 3–4 plant structures).
teacher.function: Connecting a diagram label to the matching sentence in the text.
teacher.lower: Touch each label and read it chorally before reading the text.
teacher.onLevel: Students match each label to a sentence in the text.
teacher.challenge: Students explain why a plant needs both roots and leaves.
teacher.noTech: Students draw a plant and write the four labels.
teacher.prompt: What happens to a plant if it gets no water?

activities.title: Saturday Market
activities.skill: Completing sentences with words from a text
activities.directions: Look at the picture. Read the sentences. Choose a word for each blank.
activities.prompt: Complete the sentences with words from the text.
passage: Mrs. Osei and her son Kofi go to the market on Saturday.
They buy red apples and yellow corn.
Kofi carries the basket.

picture.alt: A woman and a boy at a market stand with red apples and yellow corn. The boy holds a basket.

segments.text: At the market, they buy red
and yellow
. Kofi carries the

a place where people buy and sell food and things
mercado: un lugar donde la gente compra y vende comida y cosas
buy
to get something by paying money
comprar: obtener algo pagando dinero
basket
a container for carrying things
canasta: un recipiente para llevar cosas
activities.correct: You did it! Red apples, yellow corn, and Kofi carries the basket — all from the text and the picture.
activities.hint: Read sentence 2. Which food is red? Which food is yellow?
activities.support: Find each color word in the text. The food word comes right after it.

teacher.prompt: What foods do families in your home country buy at a market?

activities.title: A Day at the Park
activities.skill: Choosing two details from a text and picture
activities.directions: Look at the picture. Read the sentences. Choose TWO answers.
activities.prompt: Which TWO things are in the park? Choose two.
passage: It is Saturday at the park.
Luis and Fatima kick a soccer ball.
A brown dog runs on the grass.
Grandpa sits on a bench and smiles.

picture.alt: Two children kick a soccer ball on the grass in a park. A brown dog runs nearby, and a grandfather sits on a bench under a tree.

vocabulary: park
an outdoor place with grass and trees where people play
parque: un lugar al aire libre con pasto y árboles donde la gente juega
kick
to hit something with your foot
patear: golpear algo con el pie
bench
a long seat for two or more people
banca: un asiento largo para dos o más personas
frames: In the park, there is a ___ and a ___.
activities.correct: Yes! The text and the picture show a dog on the grass and a bench where Grandpa sits.
activities.hint: Read each sentence. Which things from the answers do you see in the text?
activities.support: Point to the dog and the bench in the picture. Is there a bus or a cake?
activities.extension: What else is in the park? Write: There is a ___ in the park.

teacher.use: First multi-select practice: choose two details that are in the text.
teacher.function: Locating more than one detail; rejecting details not in the text.
teacher.lower: Read each answer choice aloud and ask: Is it in the picture? Thumbs up or down.
teacher.onLevel: Students choose two answers and point to the sentences that prove them.
teacher.challenge: Students write two sentences about what Luis and Fatima do.
teacher.noTech: Students circle two things in the printed picture that match the text.
teacher.prompt: What do you like to do at the park on the weekend?

activities.title: A Tree in Four Seasons
activities.skill: Using a picture and text to find a detail
activities.directions: Look at the pictures of the tree. Read the sentences. Choose the best answer.
activities.prompt: When does the tree have no leaves?
passage: This tree changes in every season.
In fall, the leaves turn orange and fall down.
In winter, the tree has no leaves at all.

picture.alt: The same tree in four seasons: pink flowers in spring, green leaves in summer, orange leaves falling in fall, and bare branches with snow in winter.

vocabulary: season
one of the four parts of the year
estación: una de las cuatro partes del año
fall
the season when leaves change color (also called autumn)
otoño: la estación cuando las hojas cambian de color
winter
the coldest season of the year
invierno: la estación más fría del año
activities.correct: Right! The text says in winter the tree has no leaves, and the winter picture shows bare branches with snow.
activities.hint: Find the words no leaves in the text. Which season word is in that sentence?
activities.support: In fall the leaves are falling, but some are still there. Look at the picture with snow.
activities.extension: Write a sentence about the tree in spring.

teacher.use: Picture-supported detail question with a science/seasons topic.
teacher.function: Locating a detail; distinguishing fall (leaves falling) from winter (no leaves).
teacher.lower: Name each season panel together and describe the leaves in each one.
teacher.onLevel: Students answer and explain why fall is not the answer.
teacher.challenge: Students describe how the tree looks in each of the four seasons.
teacher.noTech: Fold a paper in four; students draw and label the tree in each season.
teacher.prompt: Which season is your favorite? Why?

activities.title: A Rainy Morning
activities.skill: Finding a cause
activities.directions: Look at the picture. Read the sentences. Choose the best answer.
activities.prompt: Why does Ana open her umbrella?
passage: It is raining this morning.
Ana opens her red umbrella.
She waits for the school bus with her dad.

picture.alt: A girl holds a red umbrella in the rain next to her dad at a bus stop. A yellow school bus is coming down the street.

vocabulary: umbrella
a cover you hold over your head in the rain
paraguas: algo que sostienes sobre la cabeza cuando llueve
raining
water is falling from the clouds
lloviendo: el agua cae de las nubes
wait
to stay until something comes
esperar: quedarse hasta que algo llegue
activities.correct: Yes! It is raining, so Ana opens her umbrella. That is a cause (rain) and an effect (umbrella).
activities.hint: Read the first sentence. What is the weather?
activities.support: Look at the drops falling in the picture. What do people use when it rains?
activities.extension: Finish the sentence: When it is sunny, Ana ___.

teacher.use: Introduces simple cause and effect with because.
teacher.function: Explaining why with because; linking weather to an action.
teacher.lower: Act it out: say 'It is raining!' and open a pretend umbrella.
teacher.onLevel: Students answer and say the full because sentence.
teacher.challenge: Students write another cause/effect pair about weather.
teacher.noTech: Students draw what Ana does on a sunny day and write a because sentence.
teacher.prompt: What do you wear or carry when it rains?

activities.title: Our Favorite Fruit
activities.skill: Reading a pictograph
activities.directions: Read the sentences. Look at the chart. Choose the best answer.
activities.prompt: Which fruit got the most votes?
passage: Room 12 voted for their favorite fruit.
Each child picked one fruit.
Each face on the chart is one child.
vocabulary: vote
to choose one thing from a list
votar: escoger una cosa de una lista
most
the biggest number
la mayoría (más): el número más grande
chart
a picture that shows numbers
gráfica: un dibujo que muestra números
readFor: the longest row on the chart
activities.correct: Correct! Grapes has 7 faces — the longest row — so grapes got the most votes.
activities.hint: Count the faces in each row. Which row is the longest?
activities.support: Touch and count each face: apples 5, bananas 3. Keep counting the other rows.
activities.extension: Which fruit got the fewest votes? Write: ___ got the fewest votes.

teacher.use: Pictograph reading, linked to Grade 3 data standards.
teacher.function: Comparing quantities; using most/fewest.
teacher.lower: Count each row aloud together; write the number at the end of each row.
teacher.onLevel: Students answer and tell how many votes the winning fruit got.
teacher.challenge: Students tell how many more children chose grapes than apples.
teacher.noTech: Run a real class vote and build a sticky-note pictograph.
teacher.prompt: What is your favorite fruit? Would it win in our class?

activities.title: Class Pets

activities.directions: Read the sentences. Look at the table. Choose a word for each blank.
activities.prompt: Use the table to complete the sentences.
passage: Mr. Haddad's students have many pets at home.

segments.text: Six students have a
. Four students have a
. Only one student has a

activities.extension: How many students have a fish? Write a sentence.

teacher.use: Reading rows in a two-column table.
teacher.function: Matching number words (six, four, one) to numerals and labels.
teacher.lower: Review number words six, four, one with fingers before reading.
teacher.onLevel: Students complete the cloze and read each sentence aloud.
teacher.challenge: Students write a sentence comparing two pets (more/fewer).
teacher.noTech: Copy the table on the board; students survey their own class pets.
teacher.prompt: Do you have a pet, or what pet would you like?

activities.title: Good Night, Sky

bright

window

teacher.onLevel: Students click the line and explain which word helped.
teacher.challenge: Students write a fifth line that rhymes with night.

teacher.prompt: What do you see when you look out of your window at night?

activities.prompt: Put the steps of the water cycle in order, starting with evaporation.
passage: The water on Earth is always moving. The same water has been used again and again for millions of years. Its journey from the ground to the sky and back again is called the water cycle.
Evaporation: When the sun heats water in oceans, lakes, and rivers, some of the water turns into an invisible gas called water vapor. The vapor rises up into the air.
Condensation: High in the sky, the air is cooler. The water vapor cools down and turns back into tiny drops of water. Millions of these drops join together to form clouds.
Precipitation: When the drops in a cloud get too big and heavy, they fall to the ground. This is called precipitation. It can be rain, snow, sleet, or hail, depending on how cold the air is.
Collection: The water collects in oceans, lakes, and rivers, or it soaks into the ground. Then the sun heats it again, and the cycle starts all over.
Caption: The picture shows water rising from a lake, forming a cloud, and falling back down as rain.

activities.title: From Seed to Bean Plant: Life Cycle Order
activities.skill: Putting the stages of a life cycle in order
activities.directions: Read the text about the life cycle of a bean plant. Put the stages in the order they happen.
activities.prompt: What is the order of the bean plant's life cycle?
passage: Every bean plant begins as a seed. A bean seed can be white, brown, black, or red, depending on the kind. Inside the seed's hard coat are a tiny baby plant and stored food. When the seed gets water and warmth, it begins to germinate. The seed swells, the coat splits, and a root grows down into the soil. Next, a green shoot pushes up toward the light.

Once the shoot reaches the air, its leaves open and begin to make food from sunlight, air, and water. The young plant is now called a seedling. As the seedling grows taller, it grows more leaves and a stronger stem. After several weeks, it becomes an adult plant and grows flowers.

After a flower dies, a bean pod starts to grow in its place. Inside the pod are new seeds. When the pod dries, the seeds can fall to the ground or be planted by people, and the life cycle begins again. Sara planted a bean seed in a cup of soil and measured her plant every week.
